passages.context: Conditional probability of an event given another event is defined by an intersection-to-conditioning-event probability ratio, with a strictly positive denominator.
passages.supports: This form is used for the same mathematical concept in contextual Indonesian exposition.
passages.does_not_establish: A sole nationally preferred form, an introductory/specialist register split, or validation of every target occurrence.

passages.context: The named definition is a cumulative distribution function; the later function assigns probabilities to individual discrete values.
passages.supports: Context distinguishes a cumulative function from a discrete mass assignment despite overlapping lexical roots.
passages.does_not_establish: Equivalence of cumulative distribution, general probability law and arbitrary probability functions. Neighboring theorem typography is not certified.

passages.context: A Bernoulli variable is assigned probabilities of success and failure, followed by its two-point mass formula.
passages.supports: The alternative lexical root also appears in a formal mathematical definition within the same university text.
passages.does_not_establish: A unique curriculum-wide preferred designation. The unrelated moment formulas elsewhere on this page are not certified.
